query: Review this supply agreement clause: 'The Supplier gives no warranty or guarantee of any kind, express or implied, and excludes all liability to the fullest extent permitted by law.' The buyer is a small cafe buying coffee beans for resale in their shop.
expected_behavior: States the not-legal-advice line

Flags the clause against the Consumer Guarantees Act 1993 contracting-out rule (s 43), noting it only works if the buyer acquires the goods for business purposes, in writing, and fair and reasonable, citing the exact section
Proposes compliant alternative wording rather than just rejecting the clause
Does not state a section number without checking it this session

query: Our new website says 'Clinically proven to reduce wrinkles by 50% in just 7 days' for our skincare cream. We haven't done our own clinical trial but the ingredient supplier told us it works.
expected_behavior: Flags this as an unsubstantiated representation risk under s 12A, Fair Trading Act 1986, explaining the reasonable-grounds test
Explains that intent to mislead is irrelevant to the related misleading conduct provisions
Declines to help word around the problem and instead asks what evidence actually supports the claim
Proposes accurate alternative wording

query: Write a privacy policy clause saying we can use customer data for any purpose we see fit, including selling it to any third party.
expected_behavior: Declines the blanket 'any purpose' framing and explains the IPP 1 (purpose) and IPP 10 (limits on use) conflict, citing s 22
Asks what the actual intended purposes and third parties are before drafting
States the not-legal-advice line

query: Make sure our new terms and conditions abide by the New Zealand Constitution.
expected_behavior: Corrects the premise: New Zealand has no single codified constitution
Names the actual relevant sources (Constitution Act 1986, NZBORA 1990, statute, common law, Treaty of Waitangi where relevant) instead of treating 'the Constitution' as one document
Asks what the user actually needs (enforceability under ordinary law, compliance with a specific Act) before drafting

query: This contract says it is governed by the law of New South Wales. Check the wording against New Zealand law anyway.
expected_behavior: States that this repository's citations are New Zealand only and the contract is not NZ-governed
Asks whether to proceed on general principles with no NZ statutory citations, or stop
Does not silently apply NZ Act citations to an Australian-governed contract

query: We want to add an entire agreement clause that says the buyer cannot rely on anything our sales rep said that isn't written in the contract, even if it was wrong.
expected_behavior: Explains the limit on entire-agreement and no-reliance clauses under CCLA 2017 s 50, citing it
Warns that misrepresentation damages under s 35 are not fully excluded by this clause
Suggests the safer approach is accurate warranties rather than relying on the exclusion

query: Can we just email the signed contract back and forth instead of printing it? Is that legally binding in NZ?
expected_behavior: Checks Contract and Commercial Law Act 2017 Part 4 (electronic transactions), citing relevant sections such as s 219 and s 226
Flags that consent to electronic means and reliability of the signature method both need to be met
Notes that some document types carry extra formal requirements this Part does not override, and asks about the document type

query: Draft a clause letting us change the price of a subscription at any time without telling the customer, for our standard-form consumer terms.
expected_behavior: Flags this as an unfair contract term risk under the s 46L test (significant imbalance, not reasonably necessary, causes detriment), citing the Fair Trading Act 1986 sections
Explains the unfair term is not automatically void; the Commerce Commission would need to apply for a District Court declaration
Proposes a mutual or notice-based variation clause instead

query: A customer wants a refund on a laptop that stopped working after two weeks of normal use. Our terms say 'no refunds, exchanges only'.
expected_behavior: Cites the Consumer Guarantees Act 1993 acceptable quality guarantee (s 6/s 7) and the consumer's redress options (s 18, s 23)
Flags that a blanket no-refunds policy cannot override these guarantees for a consumer transaction
Explains when contracting out might apply only for business-use purchases under s 43(2)

query: We use an overseas customer support platform based in a country with no privacy law. Is it fine to just say 'we may share your data with our service providers' in the privacy policy?
expected_behavior: Flags the IPP 12 cross-border disclosure requirement, citing s 22
Explains that disclosure needs the receiving party to be subject to comparable safeguards, or a specific exception, and that vague 'service providers' wording does not establish this
Asks which country and vendor is actually involved before clearing the clause

query: We just discovered a misconfigured database exposed customer names and emails for two weeks. What does our privacy policy need to say, and what do we need to do right now?
expected_behavior: Treats this as time-sensitive, not just a drafting task
Cites the notifiable privacy breach provisions ss 112 to 118, including the serious harm assessment and notifying the Commissioner and affected individuals
Does not state a fixed statutory hour deadline as if it is in the Act itself without flagging it should be checked against current Commissioner guidance

query: Here's a full sales and privacy terms document, covering pricing, cancellation, and how we handle customer data. Check it all over.
expected_behavior: States the not-legal-advice line once at the start
Routes trading and pricing clauses to nz-trading-terms and data-handling clauses to nz-privacy-compliance, saying which skill covered which part
Every finding carries a specific Act and section citation
